meta.ntsb_disclaimer: NTSB accident IDs in this file were matched against live NTSB data. Accident IDs cited in early project documentation (WPR13FA089, ANC12WA034, SFO08CA123) were illustrative examples and have not been verified. All matches here are from fresh live searches.

summary.note: Findings include all rules regardless of threshold. 'passed_threshold' field indicates whether combined_confidence >= 60. 'PHYSICS_ONLY' rules have ntsb_score=0 — physics validation passed but no historical accident confirmation found.

findings.interpretation: DURING CASCADE: For 'carburetor' failures with cascade duration >= 5s: during the cascade window, attention focuses on voltage=14.0–14.0 V, fuel_flow=11.0–11.0 GPH, pitch=2.45°–3.59°, altitude=4395.85–12674.85 ft. voltage IQR=0.00V — minimal electrical change in this cascade type. n=189 trajectories. | AT INJECTION (swiss cheese): For 'carburetor' failures: the most discriminating pre-existing conditions are fatigue(contrast=7.836), fuel_total_at_inject(contrast=7.671), pump_eff_at_inject(contrast=0.917). Catastrophic trajectories show mean P(crash)=1.00 vs recoverable P(crash)=0.00. This is the swiss cheese hole alignment pattern — these conditions at failure injection determine outcome more than any single factor alone. | GROUND TRUTH ANCHOR: Related to L1 rules R011 (FAA AC 61-23C). This relationship EXTENDS those rules: L1 encodes component-level cascade logic, but does NOT capture the 3-variable interaction (vs × pitch × alt) with pilot state (fatigue + fuel_total_at_inject + pump_eff_at_inject) that determines outcome.
